items.title: Device Code Flow: The Gift That Keeps on Giving — To Attackers
items.excerpt: Microsoft's Core Infrastructure and Security team explains why the device code flow remains a lucrative target for adversaries. The post provides architectural context, recent abuse patterns, and actionable guidance for hardening identity platforms against automated credential harvesting campaigns.

items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign
items.excerpt: A new wave of device code phishing shows how threat actors are scaling account compromise using AI and end‑to‑end automation. This campaign goes beyond traditional phishing by generating live authentication codes on demand, enabling higher success rates and sustained post‑compromise access.

items.title: Device Code Phishing is an Evolution in Identity Takeover
items.excerpt: This analysis details how device code phishing has evolved into a primary vector for identity takeover. Attackers now bypass traditional email filters by leveraging legitimate OAuth flows, forcing defenders to rethink identity monitoring and conditional access policies.

items.title: When checking the URL isn’t enough: phishing via the Microsoft identity platform | Securelist
items.excerpt: Kaspersky Securelist researchers dissect a sophisticated campaign exploiting the Microsoft identity platform. By manipulating device code flows, attackers render traditional URL inspection ineffective. The report highlights technical indicators, mitigation strategies, and the critical need for enhanced identity telemetry.

items.title: EvilTokens abuses Microsoft device code flow for account takeovers | CSO Online
items.excerpt: CSO Online examines how the EvilTokens malware family leverages Microsoft's device code authentication flow to steal credentials and maintain persistent access. The article outlines detection methods for infrastructure teams and emphasizes the risks of unmonitored OAuth token generation.

items.title: CISA and partners publish joint advisory on Russia-sponsored ...
items.excerpt: A joint CISA advisory details a Russia-sponsored phishing campaign targeting government and critical infrastructure sectors. The report outlines TTPs, compromised domains, and recommended defensive measures for network and identity administrators to mitigate state-sponsored credential theft.

items.title: The Shadow Campaigns: Uncovering Global Espionage
items.excerpt: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 reveals a series of covert espionage campaigns utilizing advanced phishing techniques and custom malware. The analysis covers infrastructure pivoting, identity compromise vectors, and long-term persistence mechanisms relevant to enterprise security operations.

items.title: Government Leaders Face Evolving Phishing Attacks
items.excerpt: StateTech Magazine explores how phishing tactics are increasingly targeting government executives through trust exploitation and personalized lures. The article discusses policy implications, training gaps, and technical controls needed to protect high-value identity accounts from compromise.

items.title: CVE-2026-18571
items.excerpt: A flaw was found in the user creation component of Keycloak when Fine-Grained Admin Permissions V2 (FGAP V2) is enabled. This issue allows a sub-administrator with permission to create users to add those users to any group, even groups the sub-administrator is not authorized to manage. This could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information or elevated privileges for the newly created users.

items.title: CVE-2026-18573
items.excerpt: A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a realm administrator configures client policies to enforce specific authentication requirements on confidential clients. items.title: CVE-2026-18572
items.excerpt: Keycloak provides authorization services that allow administrators to restrict access to resources based on time policies (for example, only allowing access during business hours). A flaw was discovered where a user can include a fake time value in their authorization request that overrides the actual server time. This allows the user to bypass these time-based restrictions and access protected resources at unauthorized times.
